abstract: To explore the impact and underlying mechanisms of setting a carbon peaking target (SCPT) on urban carbon metabolism efficiency (CME), we employed super-efficiency SBM model to measure urban CME using data from 210 cities covering the period 2005–2019. We manually collected and organized data on SCPT across various regions. We subsequently employed a staggered difference-in-differences model to examine the effect of SCPT on urban CME. The findings indicate that SCPT significantly enhances urban CME, a result that remains robust after a series of robustness and endogeneity tests. The SCPT’s impact on the CME varies depending on a city’s resource endowment, geographical location, level of marketization, and strength of the target’s temporal binding force. Mechanistic analysis demonstrates that SCPT improves urban CME by promoting green innovation and green finance. Through in-depth analysis, this study provides crucial theoretical foundations and solid empirical support for the scientific formulation and precise implementation of carbon reduction policies.

title: Does setting a carbon peak target contribute to improving carbon metabolism efficiency?

abstract: Public debt dynamics have become an important issue in modern macroeconomics, as rising debt levels pose challenges for short- and long-term growth. The role of foreign-financed debt is particularly significant because it can provide essential capital inflows while also creating potential vulnerabilities for the domestic economy. This study examines the impact of foreign-financed government debt on output growth. Using quarterly data from the U.S. from 1994 to 2025, we employ an Autoregressive Distributed Lag model to estimate long- and short-term relationships among variables. Our estimation results indicate that the government deficit, expressed as a percentage of GDP, positively influences output growth in the long and short run. Our short- and long-run estimation results show a negative relationship between total public debt per GDP and output growth. Our analysis also reveals that foreign-financed government debt and government expenditures positively contribute to GDP growth in the short and long run. Furthermore, the real money supply growth and the real effective exchange rate lead to a higher real GDP. Policy implications suggest that the US reserve currency advantage and deep Treasury market allow it to sustain higher foreign-financed debt to support growth. However, this U.S.-specific privilege limits the generalizability of our findings.
title: Short and long-run impacts of key fiscal variables on GDP in the USA: does foreign-financed debt matter for output growth?

abstract: This study delves into the bidirectional link between Algorithmic Trading and intraday tail risk. It reveals that both Proprietary and Agency Algorithmic Traders (ATs), through their order placements and cancellations, contribute to lowering intraday tail risk. Interestingly, this relationship is two-sided: tail risk reduces order activity across trader types. While order placements by all ATs (Proprietary, Agency, and Retail ATs) decrease with rising tail risk, only Agency ATs’ cancellations exhibit the same trend. These findings reveal heterogeneity in risk sensitivities and trading responses among ATs.
title: Trading in the Shadows: can Algo Trading amplify intraday tail risk?
title_zh: 暗影中的交易：算法交易会放大日内尾部风险吗？

abstract: Economic analysis based on text data has expanded rapidly, yet the ultra-high dimensionality of text data presents substantial challenges for term selection and estimation. We propose the Information-Adaptive Lasso and Information-Adaptive Spike-and-Slab Lasso as novel frequentist and Bayesian approaches to address these challenges. A key theoretical contribution of this study is the establishment of the rate of convergence in term-selection consistency, which we show to be faster than those achieved in the existing Lasso literature. Applying our methods to Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) statements, we identify and estimate high-impact terms driving fluctuations in monetary policy uncertainty.
abstract_zh: 基于文本数据的经济分析发展迅速，然而文本数据的超高维度给术语选择和估计带来了巨大挑战。我们提出了信息自适应Lasso和信息自适应尖峰- slab Lasso，作为应对这些挑战的新型频率学派和贝叶斯方法。本研究的一个关键理论贡献是确立了术语选择一致性的收敛速率，我们证明该速率快于现有Lasso文献中所达到的速率。将我们的方法应用于联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）声明，我们识别并估计了驱动货币政策不确定性波动的高影响力术语。
title: Text-term selection and analysis: Frequentist and Bayesian strategies and interpretations
title_zh: 文本项选择与分析：频率学派与贝叶斯策略及解释

abstract: Using detailed data from the introduction of a new high‐value payment system (HVPS) in Canada, we show how participants learn to use the new gridlock resolution arrangement to create gridlock and save liquidity. These observed behaviors are consistent with the equilibrium of a “gridlock game” that captures the key incentives participants face in the system. The findings have important implications for the design of HVPSs and shed light on financial institutions' liquidity preference.
abstract_zh: 利用加拿大引入新型高价值支付系统（HVPS）的详细数据，我们展示了参与者如何学会利用新的僵局解决机制来制造僵局并节省流动性。这些观察到的行为与“僵局博弈”的均衡状态相符，该博弈捕捉了参与者在系统中面临的关键激励。研究结果对HVPS的设计具有重要意义，并揭示了金融机构的流动性偏好。
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title: How Banks Create Gridlock in Payment Systems to Save Liquidity: The Case of Canada
title_zh: 银行如何在支付系统中制造僵局以节省流动性：加拿大案例
